name: CI / CD | Reusable pipelines
tagline: GitHub Actions workflows and bash scripts reused across my projects, from Docker Swarm deployments to npm and browser store releases.
popTagline: Reusable GitHub Actions pipelines for deploying applications and releasing packages.
popOverview: A collection of Bash generators and shared workflow templates designed to standardize CI/CD across my projects. It covers Docker-based website deployments, npm publishing and browser extension releases, while adapting to both standalone repositories and monorepos.

sectionKeyPoints.Promotion: Image tags are injected into the generated stack file, and production reuses the tags validated in staging.

sectionKeyPoints.Branch flow: Pull requests to the main branch can be restricted to staging, which is recreated after each release.

sectionKeyPoints.Release guards: The tag must be on the main branch and match the package version; files of failed deployments are archived with a timestamp.

sectionKeyPoints.Promote, don't rebuild: Production deploys the exact images validated in staging, by copying their tags.

sectionKeyPoints.Health checks, then rollback: Replica counts are polled after deploying; if services aren't healthy in time, the previous stack file is restored and deployed again.

sectionKeyPoints.Scripts on both sides: Job scripts run on the CI runner, deployment scripts on the server: each side can also be run by hand.

sectionKeyPoints.Keeping copies in sync: Scripts are reused by copying them, so improvements are carried over by hand from one repository to another.

sectionKeyPoints.Keeping actions up to date: GitHub retiring Node 20 for actions meant moving every workflow to newer action versions, and pinning the runner images.

sectionKeyPoints.Making failure a non-event: A failed deployment has to be detected, rolled back and archived: the rollback path is what makes frequent deployments comfortable.
